import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Homological conjectures in commutative algebra

A collection of interrelated statements connecting homological properties of modules over
Noetherian rings with dimension, depth, and regularity.

*Reference:*
[Wikipedia, Homological conjectures in commutative algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra)
-/

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits IsLocalRing
open RingTheory.Sequence

namespace HomologicalConjecturesInCommutativeAlgebra

universe u

/-- The projective dimension of an `R`-module, valued in `ℕ∞`. It is the least length of a
bounded projective resolution, or `⊤` if no bounded projective resolution exists. -/
noncomputable def projectiveDimension {R M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf ({⊤} ∪ {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of R M)),
    n = k ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, k < i → IsZero (P.complex.X i)})

/-- A system of parameters in a local ring is a list whose length is the dimension of the ring
and whose generated ideal is primary for the maximal ideal. -/
def IsSystemOfParameters {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (xs : List R) : Prop :=
  (xs.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧
    (Ideal.ofList xs).radical = maximalIdeal R

/-- A Noetherian local ring is Cohen--Macaulay when a system of parameters is a regular
sequence. -/
def IsCohenMacaulayLocal (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop :=
  ∃ xs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters xs ∧ IsRegular R xs

/-- A ring is Cohen--Macaulay when its localization at every prime ideal is Cohen--Macaulay. -/
def IsCohenMacaulayRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], IsCohenMacaulayLocal (Localization.AtPrime p)

/-- A local ring is regular when its maximal ideal can be generated by as many elements as the
Krull dimension of the ring. -/
def IsRegularLocal (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop :=
  ∃ xs : List R, (xs.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧
    Ideal.ofList xs = maximalIdeal R

/-- A ring is regular when its localization at every prime ideal is a regular local ring. -/
def IsRegularRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], IsRegularLocal (Localization.AtPrime p)

/-- A module is balanced big Cohen--Macaulay if its maximal-ideal multiple is proper and every
system of parameters is weakly regular on it. -/
def IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay {R W : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W] : Prop :=
  maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R W) ≠ ⊤ ∧
    ∀ xs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters xs → IsWeaklyRegular W xs

/-- A linear map exhibits its domain as a direct summand if it has a linear left inverse. -/
def IsLinearRetract {R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N]
    [Module R M] [Module R N] (i : M →ₗ[R] N) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : N →ₗ[R] M, r.comp i = LinearMap.id

/-- A submodule `P` is a direct summand of `Q` under a linear map if the restricted map from
`P` to `Q` has a linear left inverse. -/
def IsDirectSummandUnder {R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N]
    [Module R M] [Module R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (P : Submodule R M)
    (Q : Submodule R N) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : P.map f ≤ Q,
    IsLinearRetract ((f.domRestrict P).codRestrict Q fun x ↦ h (Submodule.mem_map_of_mem x.2))

/-- A chain complex is concentrated in degrees `0, ..., n` and consists of finite free
modules. -/
def IsFiniteFreeComplexOfLength {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ)
    (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Free R (G.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (G.X i)) ∧
    ∀ i : ℕ, n < i → IsZero (G.X i)

/-- The homology of a bounded complex has finite length and is not identically zero. -/
def HasFiniteLengthNonzeroHomology {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ)
    (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : ℕ, IsFiniteLength R (G.homology i)) ∧
    ∃ i ≤ n, Nontrivial (G.homology i)

/-- The positive homology groups have finite length, while the zeroth homology has a minimal
generator killed by a power of the maximal ideal. -/
def HasImprovedIntersectionHomology {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsFiniteLength R (G.homology i)) ∧
    ∃ z : G.homology 0,
      z ∉ maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R (G.homology 0)) ∧
      ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ (maximalIdeal R) ^ k, a • z = 0

/-- A ring homomorphism `g : R →+* S`, following `f : A →+* R`, regarded as an `A`-linear
map. -/
def linearMapOfRingHomComp {A R S : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : A →+* R) (g : R →+* S) :
    letI : Module A R := Module.compHom R f
    letI : Module A S := Module.compHom S (g.comp f)
    R →ₗ[A] S := by
  letI : Module A R := Module.compHom R f
  letI : Module A S := Module.compHom S (g.comp f)
  exact
    { toFun := g
      map_add' := g.map_add
      map_smul' := fun a s ↦ by
        change g (f a * s) = g (f a) * g s
        rw [map_mul] }

/-- Serre's intersection multiplicity, computed from the Tor groups through degree `d`. -/
noncomputable def intersectionMultiplicity {R M N : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (d : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (d + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ i *
    (Module.length R (((CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat R) i).obj
      (ModuleCat.of R M)).obj (ModuleCat.of R N))).toNat

namespace parts

/-- **The Zero Divisor Theorem.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and `M` a nonzero finite
`R`-module of finite projective dimension. If `r` is a non-zero-divisor on `M`, then `r` is a
non-zero-divisor on `R`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem i {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : projectiveDimension (R := R) (M := M) ≠ ⊤) (r : R)
    (hr : IsSMulRegular M r) : IsSMulRegular R r := by
  sorry

/-- **The Intersection Theorem.** Let `M` and `N` be finite modules over a Noetherian local
ring `R`. If `M ⊗[R] N` is nonzero and has finite length, then the dimension of `N`, equivalently
that of `R / Ann(N)`, is at most the projective dimension of `M`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem iii {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hnonzero : Nontrivial (TensorProduct R M N))
    (hlength : IsFiniteLength R (TensorProduct R M N)) :
    Module.supportDim R N ≤ (projectiveDimension (R := R) (M := M) : WithBot ℕ∞) := by
  sorry

/-- **The New Intersection Theorem.** If a chain complex
`0 → Gₙ → ... → G₀ → 0` of finite free modules over a Noetherian local ring has finite-length,
nonzero total homology, then `dim R ≤ n`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem iv {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ)
    (hfree : IsFiniteFreeComplexOfLength n G)
    (hhomology : HasFiniteLengthNonzeroHomology n G) : ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/-- **The Improved New Intersection Conjecture.** Let
`0 → Gₙ → ... → G₀ → 0` be a complex of finite free modules over a Noetherian local ring.
Suppose every positive homology group has finite length and `H₀` has an element outside
`m H₀` killed by a power of `m`. Then `dim R ≤ n`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem v {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ)
    (hfree : IsFiniteFreeComplexOfLength n G)
    (hhomology : HasImprovedIntersectionHomology G) : ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/-- **The Direct Summand Conjecture.** If `R ⊆ S` is an injective module-finite extension of
Noetherian rings and `R` is regular, then the inclusion has an `R`-linear retraction. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem vi {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) (hregular : IsRegularRing R) :
    IsLinearRetract (Algebra.linearMap R S) := by
  sorry

/-- **Existence of Balanced Big Cohen--Macaulay Modules.** Every Noetherian local ring `R`
has an `R`-module `W`, not necessarily finite, such that `mW ≠ W` and every system of parameters
is weakly regular on `W`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem viii {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    ∃ (W : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup W) (_ : Module R W),
      IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (R := R) (W := W) := by
  sorry

/-- **Cohen--Macaulayness of Direct Summands.** Let `R ⊆ S` be an injective extension of
Noetherian rings. If `S` is regular and the inclusion has an `R`-linear retraction, then `R` is
Cohen--Macaulay. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem ix {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) (hregular : IsRegularRing S)
    (hretract : IsLinearRetract (Algebra.linearMap R S)) : IsCohenMacaulayRing R := by
  sorry

/-- **The Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor.** Let `A ⊆ R → S`, where `A` and `S` are
regular Noetherian rings, `A → R` is injective, and `R` is finite as an `A`-module. For every
`A`-module `W`, the induced map `Torᵢᴬ(W,R) → Torᵢᴬ(W,S)` is zero for every `i ≥ 1`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem x {A R S W : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W] (f : A →+* R) (g : R →+* S)
    (hinj : Function.Injective f)
    (hfinite : letI : Module A R := Module.compHom R f; Module.Finite A R)
    (hA : IsRegularRing A) (hS : IsRegularRing S) :
    letI : Module A R := Module.compHom R f
    letI : Module A S := Module.compHom S (g.comp f)
    ∀ i ≥ 1,
      ((CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat A) i).obj (ModuleCat.of A W)).map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (linearMapOfRingHomComp f g)) = 0 := by
  sorry

/-- **The Strong Direct Summand Conjecture.** Let `R ⊆ S` be an injective module-finite map of
complete Noetherian local domains. Let `Q` be a height-one prime of `S` lying over `xR`, and
suppose `R` and `R/xR` are regular. Then `xR` is a direct summand of `Q` as an `R`-module. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem xi {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S]
    [Module.Finite R S] (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (x : R) (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime] (hheight : Q.height = 1)
    (hliesOver : Q.comap (algebraMap R S) = Ideal.span {x})
    (hR : IsRegularLocal R) (_ : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}))
    (hRx : IsRegularLocal (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})) :
    IsDirectSummandUnder (Algebra.linearMap R S) (Ideal.span {x})
      (Q.restrictScalars R) := by
  sorry

/-- **Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen--Macaulay Algebras.** For every local map
`R → S` of complete Noetherian local domains, there are balanced big Cohen--Macaulay algebras
`B_R` and `B_S` and a map `B_R → B_S` commuting with the structure maps from `R`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem xii {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] :
    ∃ (BR : Type) (_ : CommRing BR) (_ : Algebra R BR),
      IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (R := R) (W := BR) ∧
      ∃ (BS : Type) (_ : CommRing BS) (_ : Algebra S BS),
        IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (R := S) (W := BS) ∧
        ∃ g : BR →+* BS,
          g.comp (algebraMap R BR) = (algebraMap S BS).comp (algebraMap R S) := by
  sorry

/-- **Serre's Conjecture on Multiplicities.** Let `R` be a regular Noetherian local ring of
dimension `d`, and let `M` and `N` be finite `R`-modules whose tensor product has finite length.
The alternating sum `χ(M,N)` of the lengths of their Tor groups is zero if
`dim M + dim N < d`, and is positive if `dim M + dim N = d`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem xiii {R M N : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (d : ℕ) (hregular : IsRegularLocal R)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hlength : IsFiniteLength R (TensorProduct R M N)) :
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N < (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      intersectionMultiplicity (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) d = 0) ∧
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      0 < intersectionMultiplicity (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) d) := by
  sorry

/-- **The Small Cohen--Macaulay Modules Conjecture.** Every complete Noetherian local ring has
a nonzero finite module on which some system of parameters is a regular sequence. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem xiv {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] :
    ∃ (M : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M) (_ : Module.Finite R M),
      Nontrivial M ∧
      ∃ xs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters (R := R) xs ∧ IsRegular M xs := by
  sorry

end parts

end HomologicalConjecturesInCommutativeAlgebra
modeling_decisions: Applied the article's global preamble: R is Noetherian local and M,N are finite R-modules in the local statements; A,R,S are Noetherian in the nonlocal statements.
Defined a system of parameters as a list of length dim R whose generated ideal has radical equal to the maximal ideal.
Used Mathlib's IsWeaklyRegular for balanced big Cohen–Macaulay objects, keeping mW ≠ W as a separate condition as requested.
Defined a regular local ring by generation of its maximal ideal by dim R elements, and global regularity by regularity of every prime localization.
Defined local Cohen–Macaulayness by existence of a system of parameters regular on R, and global Cohen–Macaulayness through all prime localizations.
Defined projective dimension in ℕ∞ as the infimum of finite bounds on projective resolutions, with ⊤ included so modules with no bounded resolution have infinite dimension.

For the New Intersection Theorem, represented 0 → G_n → ... → G_0 → 0 as an ℕ-indexed ChainComplex with zero objects above n. Under this boundedness, finite length of the direct sum of homology is represented by finite length in every degree, and nonzero total homology by a nontrivial homology group in some degree at most n.
Interpreted a minimal generator killed by a power of m as z ∉ mH₀ together with m^k z = 0 for some k.
Used IsAdicComplete at the maximal ideal for completeness of Noetherian local rings.
In the Strong Direct Summand Conjecture, made the quotient's local-ring structure explicit; this includes the properness/nontriviality implicit in saying R/xR is regular.
For maps of Tor, used CategoryTheory.Tor on ModuleCat and the A-linear map underlying R → S. The involved types share a universe, as required by this categorical API.
For Serre multiplicity, summed Tor lengths from degree 0 through d. This is the full Euler characteristic because a regular local ring of dimension d has global dimension d.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution and CategoryTheory.Tor

homological_conjectures_in_commutative_a.why: Uses a projective-dimension definition valued in ℕ∞, defined as the least bound of a categorical projective resolution.

Mathlib has no injective-resolution or injective-dimension API for modules. Faithfully expressing 'finite injective resolution' would require a substantial bespoke dual resolution theory, rather than a statement-level definition.
Uses the bespoke projectiveDimension definition and Mathlib's Module.supportDim, which equals dim(R/ann N) for finite modules.
Uses predicates for a bounded finite-free ChainComplex and for finite-length nonzero homology.
Uses bespoke standard local/global predicates for regular and Cohen–Macaulay rings and a linear-retraction predicate.
Uses predicates for a bounded finite-free complex and for an H₀ element outside mH₀ annihilated by a power of m.
Uses a small predicate saying that the algebra's canonical R-linear map has a linear left inverse.

Mathlib does not define the Koszul complex. A faithful statement also needs its canonical top-degree identification and chain-map lift into a free resolution; recreating that machinery locally would be substantial and error-prone.
Uses bespoke predicates for systems of parameters and balanced big Cohen–Macaulay modules, with Mathlib's IsWeaklyRegular for the requested weak regularity.
Uses Mathlib's categorical Tor on ModuleCat, plus a helper making R → S into the induced A-linear map and a standard bespoke regular-ring predicate.
Uses adic completeness, ideal height/comap, standard local regularity, and a predicate for the restricted map xR → Q having an R-linear left inverse.
Uses the balanced big Cohen–Macaulay predicate; the commuting square is stated as equality of composed ring homomorphisms.
Defines χ as the alternating integer sum of Tor lengths through d; for a regular local ring of dimension d, higher Tor groups vanish.
Uses adic completeness and the bespoke system-of-parameters predicate together with Mathlib's regular-sequence predicate.

/-- **The Zero Divisor Theorem.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and `M` a nonzero finite
`R`-module of finite projective dimension. If `r` is a non-zero-divisor on `M`, then `r` is a
non-zero-divisor on `R`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem i {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : projectiveDimension (R := R) (M := M) ≠ ⊤) (r : R)
    (hr : IsSMulRegular M r) : IsSMulRegular R r := by
  sorry

/-- **The Intersection Theorem.** Let `M` and `N` be finite modules over a Noetherian local
ring `R`. If `M ⊗[R] N` is nonzero and has finite length, then the dimension of `N`, equivalently
that of `R / Ann(N)`, is at most the projective dimension of `M`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem iii {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hnonzero : Nontrivial (TensorProduct R M N))
    (hlength : IsFiniteLength R (TensorProduct R M N)) :
    Module.supportDim R N ≤ (projectiveDimension (R := R) (M := M) : WithBot ℕ∞) := by
  sorry

/-- **The New Intersection Theorem.** If a chain complex
`0 → Gₙ → ... → G₀ → 0` of finite free modules over a Noetherian local ring has finite-length,
nonzero total homology, then `dim R ≤ n`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem iv {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ)
    (hfree : IsFiniteFreeComplexOfLength n G)
    (hhomology : HasFiniteLengthNonzeroHomology n G) : ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/-- **Cohen--Macaulayness of Direct Summands.** Let `R ⊆ S` be an injective extension of
Noetherian rings. If `S` is regular and the inclusion has an `R`-linear retraction, then `R` is
Cohen--Macaulay. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem ix {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) (hregular : IsRegularRing S)
    (hretract : IsLinearRetract (Algebra.linearMap R S)) : IsCohenMacaulayRing R := by
  sorry

/-- **The Improved New Intersection Conjecture.** Let
`0 → Gₙ → ... → G₀ → 0` be a complex of finite free modules over a Noetherian local ring.
Suppose every positive homology group has finite length and `H₀` has an element outside
`m H₀` killed by a power of `m`. Then `dim R ≤ n`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem v {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ)
    (hfree : IsFiniteFreeComplexOfLength n G)
    (hhomology : HasImprovedIntersectionHomology G) : ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/-- **The Direct Summand Conjecture.** If `R ⊆ S` is an injective module-finite extension of
Noetherian rings and `R` is regular, then the inclusion has an `R`-linear retraction. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem vi {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) (hregular : IsRegularRing R) :
    IsLinearRetract (Algebra.linearMap R S) := by
  sorry

/-- **Existence of Balanced Big Cohen--Macaulay Modules.** Every Noetherian local ring `R`
has an `R`-module `W`, not necessarily finite, such that `mW ≠ W` and every system of parameters
is weakly regular on `W`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem viii {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    ∃ (W : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup W) (_ : Module R W),
      IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (R := R) (W := W) := by
  sorry

/-- **The Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor.** Let `A ⊆ R → S`, where `A` and `S` are
regular Noetherian rings, `A → R` is injective, and `R` is finite as an `A`-module. For every
`A`-module `W`, the induced map `Torᵢᴬ(W,R) → Torᵢᴬ(W,S)` is zero for every `i ≥ 1`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem x {A R S W : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W] (f : A →+* R) (g : R →+* S)
    (hinj : Function.Injective f)
    (hfinite : letI : Module A R := Module.compHom R f; Module.Finite A R)
    (hA : IsRegularRing A) (hS : IsRegularRing S) :
    letI : Module A R := Module.compHom R f
    letI : Module A S := Module.compHom S (g.comp f)
    ∀ i ≥ 1,
      ((CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat A) i).obj (ModuleCat.of A W)).map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (linearMapOfRingHomComp f g)) = 0 := by
  sorry

/-- **The Strong Direct Summand Conjecture.** Let `R ⊆ S` be an injective module-finite map of
complete Noetherian local domains. Let `Q` be a height-one prime of `S` lying over `xR`, and
suppose `R` and `R/xR` are regular. Then `xR` is a direct summand of `Q` as an `R`-module. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem xi {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S]
    [Module.Finite R S] (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (x : R) (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime] (hheight : Q.height = 1)
    (hliesOver : Q.comap (algebraMap R S) = Ideal.span {x})
    (hR : IsRegularLocal R) (_ : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}))
    (hRx : IsRegularLocal (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})) :
    IsDirectSummandUnder (Algebra.linearMap R S) (Ideal.span {x})
      (Q.restrictScalars R) := by
  sorry

/-- **Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen--Macaulay Algebras.** For every local map
`R → S` of complete Noetherian local domains, there are balanced big Cohen--Macaulay algebras
`B_R` and `B_S` and a map `B_R → B_S` commuting with the structure maps from `R`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem xii {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] :
    ∃ (BR : Type) (_ : CommRing BR) (_ : Algebra R BR),
      IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (R := R) (W := BR) ∧
      ∃ (BS : Type) (_ : CommRing BS) (_ : Algebra S BS),
        IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (R := S) (W := BS) ∧
        ∃ g : BR →+* BS,
          g.comp (algebraMap R BR) = (algebraMap S BS).comp (algebraMap R S) := by
  sorry

/-- **Serre's Conjecture on Multiplicities.** Let `R` be a regular Noetherian local ring of
dimension `d`, and let `M` and `N` be finite `R`-modules whose tensor product has finite length.
The alternating sum `χ(M,N)` of the lengths of their Tor groups is zero if
`dim M + dim N < d`, and is positive if `dim M + dim N = d`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem xiii {R M N : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (d : ℕ) (hregular : IsRegularLocal R)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hlength : IsFiniteLength R (TensorProduct R M N)) :
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N < (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      intersectionMultiplicity (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) d = 0) ∧
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      0 < intersectionMultiplicity (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) d) := by
  sorry

/-- **The Small Cohen--Macaulay Modules Conjecture.** Every complete Noetherian local ring has
a nonzero finite module on which some system of parameters is a regular sequence. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem xiv {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] :
    ∃ (M : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M) (_ : Module.Finite R M),
      Nontrivial M ∧
      ∃ xs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters (R := R) xs ∧ IsRegular M xs := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Homological conjectures in commutative algebra

The homological conjectures are a web of interrelated conjectures in commutative algebra.
They relate homological properties of a commutative ring to its internal structure, in
particular to its Krull dimension and depth. This file formalises the list given by
Melvin Hochster, as reproduced on Wikipedia.

Throughout, $A$, $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian commutative rings, $R$ is a local ring with maximal
ideal $\mathfrak m_R$ (except where stated otherwise), and $M$ and $N$ are finitely generated
$R$-modules.

Mathlib does not yet have depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings, regular (local) rings, systems of
parameters or Koszul complexes. This file defines them, in the local Noetherian setting of the
conjectures. The Koszul complex of $x_1, \ldots, x_d$ is built as the exterior algebra
$\bigwedge^\bullet R^d$ with the differential given by contraction against the linear form
$e_i \mapsto x_i$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Homological conjectures in commutative algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ho07] Hochster, M. "Homological conjectures, old and new." _Illinois J. Math._ 51 (2007),
  151–169.
- [An18] André, Y. "La conjecture du facteur direct." _Publ. Math. IHÉS_ 127 (2018), 71–93.
  [arXiv:1609.00345](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00345)
-/

open CategoryTheory IsLocalRing RingTheory.Sequence
open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

namespace HomologicalConjecturesInCommutativeAlgebra

/- ### Koszul complexes -/

section Koszul

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- Contraction against a linear form lowers the exterior degree by one: it maps
$\bigwedge^{n+1} M$ into $\bigwedge^n M$. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
lemma contractLeft_mem_exteriorPower (φ : Module.Dual R M) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ v ∈ ⋀[R]^(n + 1) M, CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft (Q := 0) φ v ∈ ⋀[R]^n M := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro v hv
    rw [ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower, pow_one] at hv
    obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := hv
    rw [CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι, ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower, pow_zero]
    exact Submodule.algebraMap_mem _
  | succ n ih =>
    intro v hv
    rw [ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower, pow_succ'] at hv
    refine Submodule.mul_induction_on hv (fun a ha b hb => ?_) (fun x y hx hy => ?_)
    · obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := ha
      rw [CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι_mul]
      refine Submodule.sub_mem _ (Submodule.smul_mem _ _ hb) ?_
      rw [ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower, pow_succ']
      exact Submodule.mul_mem_mul (LinearMap.mem_range_self _ m) (ih b hb)
    · rw [map_add]
      exact Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy

/-- The Koszul differential $\bigwedge^{n+1} M \to \bigwedge^n M$ attached to a linear form
$\varphi$ on $M$: contraction against $\varphi$, so that
$m_0 \wedge \cdots \wedge m_n \mapsto \sum_i (-1)^i \varphi(m_i)\,
m_0 \wedge \cdots \wedge \widehat{m_i} \wedge \cdots \wedge m_n$. -/
noncomputable def koszulD (φ : Module.Dual R M) (n : ℕ) :
    ⋀[R]^(n + 1) M →ₗ[R] ⋀[R]^n M :=
  (CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft (Q := 0) φ).restrict (contractLeft_mem_exteriorPower φ n)

/-- The Koszul differential squares to zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
lemma koszulD_comp_koszulD (φ : Module.Dual R M) (n : ℕ) :
    koszulD φ n ∘ₗ koszulD φ (n + 1) = 0 := by
  ext v
  simp [koszulD, LinearMap.restrict_apply, CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_contractLeft]

/-- In degree one, the Koszul differential $\bigwedge^1 M \to \bigwedge^0 M$ is $\varphi$ itself,
under the canonical identifications $\bigwedge^1 M = M$ and $\bigwedge^0 M = R$. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
lemma zeroEquiv_koszulD_zero (φ : Module.Dual R M) (v : ⋀[R]^1 M) :
    exteriorPower.zeroEquiv R M (koszulD φ 0 v) = φ (exteriorPower.oneEquiv R M v) := by
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := v
  rw [ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower, pow_one] at hv
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := hv
  have hm : ExteriorAlgebra.ι R m ∈ ⋀[R]^1 M := by
    simp [ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower]
  have h1 : (⟨ExteriorAlgebra.ι R m, hm⟩ : ⋀[R]^1 M) =
      exteriorPower.ιMulti R 1 (fun _ => m) := by
    ext
    simp [ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti_apply]
  have h2 : koszulD φ 0 ⟨ExteriorAlgebra.ι R m, hm⟩ =
      φ m • exteriorPower.ιMulti R 0 (fun i => i.elim0) := by
    ext
    simp [koszulD, LinearMap.restrict_apply, CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι,
      ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti_zero_apply, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one]
  rw [h2, map_smul, exteriorPower.zeroEquiv_ιMulti, h1, exteriorPower.oneEquiv_ιMulti]
  simp

/-- The Koszul complex $K_\bullet(x_1, \ldots, x_d; R)$ of the ring $R$ with respect to
$x_1, \ldots, x_d \in R$: the chain complex with $K_n = \bigwedge^n R^d$ (so $K_0 = R$,
$K_d \cong R$ and $K_n = 0$ for $n > d$), and with differential the contraction against the
linear form $R^d \to R$, $e_i \mapsto x_i$. -/
noncomputable def koszulComplex {d : ℕ} (x : Fin d → R) : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ :=
  ChainComplex.of (fun n => ModuleCat.of R (⋀[R]^n (Fin d → R)))
    (fun n => ModuleCat.ofHom (koszulD (Fintype.linearCombination R x) n))
    (fun n => by
      rw [← ModuleCat.ofHom_comp, koszulD_comp_koszulD]
      rfl)

@[category API, AMS 13]
lemma koszulComplex_X {d : ℕ} (x : Fin d → R) (n : ℕ) :
    (koszulComplex x).X n = ModuleCat.of R (⋀[R]^n (Fin d → R)) :=
  rfl

@[category API, AMS 13]
lemma koszulComplex_d {d : ℕ} (x : Fin d → R) (n : ℕ) :
    (koszulComplex x).d (n + 1) n =
      ModuleCat.ofHom (koszulD (Fintype.linearCombination R x) n) := by
  simp [koszulComplex]

end Koszul

/- ### Systems of parameters, depth, Cohen–Macaulay and regular rings -/

section Definitions

variable (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

/-- A **regular local ring**: a Noetherian local ring $R$ whose maximal ideal can be generated by
$\dim R$ elements. -/
structure IsRegularLocalRing : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R, IsLocalRing R where
  exists_finset_span_eq_maximalIdeal :
    ∃ s : Finset R,
      (s.card : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧ Ideal.span (s : Set R) = maximalIdeal R

/-- A **regular ring**: a Noetherian ring all of whose localisations at prime ideals are regular
local rings. -/
structure IsRegularRing : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization :
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)

section LocalRing

variable [IsLocalRing R]

/-- A list $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ of elements of a local ring $R$ is a **system of parameters** if
$n = \dim R$, all $x_i$ lie in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, and the ideal
$(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ is $\mathfrak m_R$-primary, i.e. $\mathfrak m_R \subseteq
\sqrt{(x_1, \ldots, x_n)}$. -/
def IsSystemOfParameters (rs : List R) : Prop :=
  (rs.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧ (∀ r ∈ rs, r ∈ maximalIdeal R) ∧
    maximalIdeal R ≤ (Ideal.ofList rs).radical

/-- The **depth** of a module $M$ over a local ring $R$: the supremum of the lengths of the
$M$-regular sequences contained in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$. -/
noncomputable def depth (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (rs : List R) (_ : ∀ r ∈ rs, r ∈ maximalIdeal R) (_ : IsRegular M rs),
    (rs.length : ℕ∞)

/-- A (not necessarily finitely generated) module $W$ over a local ring $R$ is a
**balanced big Cohen–Macaulay module** if $\mathfrak m_R W \neq W$ and every system of
parameters $x_1, \ldots, x_d$ of $R$ is a regular sequence on $W$, i.e. each $x_i$ is a
nonzerodivisor on $W / (x_1, \ldots, x_{i-1}) W$ (as $\mathfrak m_R W \neq W$, this is the same
as `IsRegular`). Applied to an $R$-algebra $B$, this is the notion of a balanced big
Cohen–Macaulay algebra. -/
def IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay (W : Type*) [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W] : Prop :=
  maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R W) ≠ ⊤ ∧
    ∀ rs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters R rs → IsWeaklyRegular W rs

end LocalRing

/-- A **Cohen–Macaulay local ring**: a Noetherian local ring $R$ with
$\operatorname{depth} R = \dim R$. -/
structure IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R, IsLocalRing R where
  depth_eq : (depth R R : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R

/-- A **Cohen–Macaulay ring**: a Noetherian ring all of whose localisations at maximal ideals are
Cohen–Macaulay local rings. -/
structure IsCohenMacaulayRing : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R where
  isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_localization :
    ∀ m : MaximalSpectrum R, IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m.asIdeal)

end Definitions

section Serre

variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R]

/-- Serre's intersection multiplicity
$$\chi(M, N) = \sum_{i = 0}^{d} (-1)^i \,\ell\bigl(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N)\bigr)$$
of two finitely generated modules $M$, $N$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension $d$. Over
such a ring $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N) = 0$ for $i > d$, so this is the full alternating sum,
and when $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length so does every $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N)$, so
that the conversion `ENat.toNat` of the lengths is lossless. -/
noncomputable def serreMultiplicity (d : ℕ) (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] : ℤ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (d + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ i *
    ((Module.length R (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R M)).obj
      (ModuleCat.of R N))).toNat : ℤ)

end Serre

/- ### The conjectures -/

section LocalConjectures

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]

/--
**The Zero Divisor Theorem.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M \neq 0$ a finitely
generated $R$-module of finite projective dimension. If $r \in R$ is not a zero divisor on $M$,
then $r$ is not a zero divisor on $R$.

Proved by Peskine–Szpiro and Roberts (it follows from the New Intersection Theorem).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.i
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : ∃ n : ℕ, HasProjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of R M) n)
    (r : R) (hr : IsSMulRegular M r) :
    IsSMulRegular R r := by
  sorry

/--
**Bass's Question.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring. If there is a finitely generated
$R$-module $M \neq 0$ of finite injective dimension (i.e. admitting a finite injective
resolution), then $R$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring.

Answered positively by Peskine–Szpiro and Roberts.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.ii
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : ∃ n : ℕ, HasInjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of R M) n) :
    IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing R := by
  sorry

/--
**The Intersection Theorem.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M$, $N$ finitely generated
$R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N \neq 0$ has finite length. Then the Krull dimension of $N$,
i.e. $\dim R / \operatorname{Ann}_R N$, is at most the projective dimension of $M$ (the bound
is vacuous if $M$ has infinite projective dimension).

Proved by Peskine–Szpiro and Roberts.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.iii
    (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hMN : Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N)) (hMN' : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N)) :
    ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R N) ≤ projectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R M) := by
  sorry

/--
**The New Intersection Theorem.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and let
$0 \to G_n \to \cdots \to G_0 \to 0$ be a finite complex of finitely generated free $R$-modules
such that $\bigoplus_i H_i(G_\bullet)$ has finite length but is not $0$. Then $\dim R \leq n$.

Proved by Roberts (1987).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.iv
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (G.X i)) (hfin : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (G.X i))
    (hn : ∀ i > n, Subsingleton (G.X i))
    (hlen : ∀ i, IsFiniteLength R (G.homology i)) (hne : ∃ i, Nontrivial (G.homology i)) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/--
**The Improved New Intersection Conjecture.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and let
$0 \to G_n \to \cdots \to G_0 \to 0$ be a finite complex of finitely generated free $R$-modules
such that $H_i(G_\bullet)$ has finite length for $i > 0$ and $H_0(G_\bullet)$ has a minimal
generator killed by a power of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, i.e. there is
$z \in H_0(G_\bullet) \setminus \mathfrak m_R H_0(G_\bullet)$ with $\mathfrak m_R^k z = 0$ for
some $k$. Then $\dim R \leq n$.

Equivalent to the Canonical Element Conjecture, hence a theorem by André's proof of the
Direct Summand Conjecture.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.v
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (G.X i)) (hfin : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (G.X i))
    (hn : ∀ i > n, Subsingleton (G.X i))
    (hlen : ∀ i > 0, IsFiniteLength R (G.homology i))
    (hgen : ∃ z : G.homology 0, z ∉ maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R (G.homology 0)) ∧
      ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ maximalIdeal R ^ k, r • z = 0) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

end LocalConjectures

/--
**The Direct Summand Conjecture.** Let $R \subseteq S$ be a module-finite ring extension with
$R$ a regular (Noetherian) ring; $R$ need not be local. Then $R$ is a direct summand of $S$ as an
$R$-module, i.e. the inclusion $R \to S$ admits an $R$-linear retraction $S \to R$.

Proved by André using perfectoid spaces [An18].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.vi
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (hR : IsRegularRing R) (hRS : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) :
    ∃ f : S →ₗ[R] R, f ∘ₗ Algebra.linearMap R S = LinearMap.id := by
  sorry

section LocalConjectures

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]

/--
**The Canonical Element Conjecture.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$ with
residue field $k$. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_d$ be a system of parameters for $R$, let $F_\bullet$ be a
free $R$-resolution of $k$ with $F_0 = R$, and let $K_\bullet = K_\bullet(x_1, \ldots, x_d; R)$
be the Koszul complex. Lift the identity map $R = K_0 \to F_0 = R$ to a map of complexes
$\alpha \colon K_\bullet \to F_\bullet$. Then, whatever the choice of system of parameters, of
resolution and of lifting, the last map $\alpha_d \colon R = K_d \to F_d$ is not $0$.

Here the identification $F_0 = R$ is an isomorphism `e`, and $K_0 = \bigwedge^0 R^d = R$ is the
canonical isomorphism `exteriorPower.zeroEquiv`; the resolution is a projective resolution all
of whose terms are free.

Equivalent to the Direct Summand Conjecture, hence a theorem by André.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.vii
    {d : ℕ} (x : Fin d → R) (hx : IsSystemOfParameters R (List.ofFn x))
    (F : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R)))
    (hF : ∀ i, Module.Free R (F.complex.X i))
    (e : F.complex.X 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of R R)
    (α : koszulComplex x ⟶ F.complex)
    (hα : α.f 0 =
      ModuleCat.ofHom (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv R (Fin d → R)).toLinearMap ≫ e.inv) :
    α.f d ≠ 0 := by
  sorry

variable (R) in
/--
**Existence of Balanced Big Cohen–Macaulay Modules Conjecture.** For every Noetherian local ring
$R$ there is a (not necessarily finitely generated) $R$-module $W$ such that
$\mathfrak m_R W \neq W$ and every system of parameters for $R$ is a regular sequence on $W$.

Proved by Hochster–Huneke in equal characteristic and by André in mixed characteristic.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.viii :
    ∃ (W : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup W) (_ : Module R W), IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay R W := by
  sorry

end LocalConjectures

/--
**Cohen–Macaulayness of Direct Summands Conjecture.** Let $R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism of
Noetherian rings with $S$ regular, such that $R$ is a direct summand of $S$ as an $R$-module,
i.e. $R \to S$ admits an $R$-linear retraction. Then $R$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring.
$R$ need not be local.

Proved by Heitmann–Ma (2018) using weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.ix
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra R S]
    (hS : IsRegularRing S)
    (hRS : ∃ f : S →ₗ[R] R, f ∘ₗ Algebra.linearMap R S = LinearMap.id) :
    IsCohenMacaulayRing R := by
  sorry

/--
**The Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor.** Let $A \subseteq R \to S$ be ring homomorphisms
with $A$ and $S$ regular (Noetherian) rings and $R$ finitely generated as an $A$-module; $R$ need
not be local. Let $W$ be any $A$-module. Then the map
$\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(W, R) \to \operatorname{Tor}_i^A(W, S)$ is zero for all $i \geq 1$.

Known in equal characteristic (Hochster–Huneke), open in mixed characteristic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.x
    (A R S : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra A R] [Algebra A S] [Algebra R S] [IsScalarTower A R S]
    (hA : IsRegularRing A) (hS : IsRegularRing S)
    (hAR : Function.Injective (algebraMap A R)) [Module.Finite A R]
    (W : Type u) [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W] (i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) :
    ((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj (ModuleCat.of A W)).map
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A R S).toLinearMap) = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
**The Strong Direct Summand Conjecture.** Let $R \subseteq S$ be a module-finite extension of
complete (Noetherian) local domains, let $x \in R$ be such that $R$ and $R / xR$ are both regular,
and let $Q$ be a height one prime ideal of $S$ lying over $xR$, i.e. $Q \cap R = xR$. Then $xR$
is a direct summand of $Q$ considered as $R$-modules, i.e. the inclusion $xR \to Q$ admits an
$R$-linear retraction $Q \to xR$.

As in the Direct Summand Conjecture that it strengthens, the extension $R \subseteq S$ is
module-finite (this is explicit in Ranganathan's formulation; without it the statement fails).

Equivalent to the Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor; open in general.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xi
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    (hR : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R) (hS : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S)
    [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S] (hRS : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (x : R) (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing R) (hreg' : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}))
    (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime] (hQ : Q.primeHeight = 1)
    (hQx : Q.comap (algebraMap R S) = Ideal.span {x}) :
    ∃ ρ : Q →ₗ[R] Ideal.span {x},
      ∀ (r : R) (h : algebraMap R S (x * r) ∈ Q),
        (ρ ⟨algebraMap R S (x * r), h⟩ : R) = x * r := by
  sorry

/--
**Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen–Macaulay Algebras Conjecture.** Let $R \to S$ be a
local homomorphism of complete (Noetherian) local domains. Then there exist an $R$-algebra $B_R$
that is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for $R$, an $S$-algebra $B_S$ that is a balanced
big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for $S$, and a ring homomorphism $B_R \to B_S$ such that the square
$R \to S \to B_S$, $R \to B_R \to B_S$ commutes.

Proved by André (2018), with contributions of Heitmann–Ma and Gabber.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xii
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    (hR : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R) (hS : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S)
    [Algebra R S] (hRS : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)) :
    ∃ (B_R : Type u) (_ : CommRing B_R) (_ : Algebra R B_R)
      (B_S : Type u) (_ : CommRing B_S) (_ : Algebra S B_S),
      IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay R B_R ∧ IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay S B_S ∧
      ∃ f : B_R →+* B_S,
        ∀ r : R, f (algebraMap R B_R r) = algebraMap S B_S (algebraMap R S r) := by
  sorry

section LocalConjectures

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]

/--
**Serre's Conjecture on Multiplicities.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring of dimension $d$ and
$M$, $N$ finitely generated $R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. Let
$\chi(M, N) = \sum_i (-1)^i \ell(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N))$. Then $\chi(M, N) = 0$ if
$\dim M + \dim N < d$, and $\chi(M, N) > 0$ if $\dim M + \dim N = d$.
(Serre proved that $\dim M + \dim N \leq d$ always holds.)

The vanishing part is a theorem of Roberts and Gillet–Soulé; the positivity part is open in
mixed characteristic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xiii
    (hR : IsRegularLocalRing R) (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim R = d)
    (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hMN : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N)) :
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N < d → serreMultiplicity R d M N = 0) ∧
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = d → 0 < serreMultiplicity R d M N) := by
  sorry

/--
**Small Cohen–Macaulay Modules Conjecture.** Let $R$ be a complete Noetherian local ring. Then
there is a finitely generated $R$-module $M \neq 0$ such that some (equivalently, every) system of
parameters for $R$ is a regular sequence on $M$.

Open in dimension at least $3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xiv
    (hR : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R) :
    ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M), Module.Finite R M ∧ Nontrivial M ∧
      ∃ rs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters R rs ∧ IsRegular M rs := by
  sorry

end LocalConjectures

end HomologicalConjecturesInCommutativeAlgebra
attempts.decomposition_objections: None of substance. Minor remarks: (1) slot xi's source text does not say 'module-finite', but the table's note (and the fact that the statement is false without it) justify including it, which I did; (2) slot vii's note says 'needs Koszul complex … machinery' — this machinery is absent from Mathlib, so I built it in the problem file rather than omitting the slot; (3) the table leaves the module universe unspecified — all asserted-to-exist modules/algebras are placed in the universe of R.
modeling_decisions: Noetherian-ness: following the article's standing convention, every ring in a statement is Noetherian; `IsRegularLocalRing`, `IsRegularRing`, `IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing`, `IsCohenMacaulayRing` are structures that bundle `IsNoetherianRing` (and `IsLocalRing` for the local ones), so e.g. `IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ span {x})` is a well-formed Prop without extra instances. In slots vi and x the intermediate ring (S resp. R) is not separately assumed Noetherian since it is module-finite over a Noetherian ring.

Regular local ring is defined as: the maximal ideal is generated by a Finset of cardinality dim R (equivalent to embdim = dim). Regular ring: all localisations at primes are regular local (Matsumura/Stacks). Cohen–Macaulay ring: all localisations at maximal ideals are CM local (Bruns–Herzog/Stacks).
Depth is defined as the supremum (in ℕ∞) of lengths of `IsRegular` sequences contained in the maximal ideal; CM local ring means depth R R = ringKrullDim R (compared in WithBot ℕ∞).
System of parameters: a `List R` of length dim R, contained in the maximal ideal, with m ≤ radical of the generated ideal (i.e. m-primary).
Balanced big Cohen–Macaulay (slots viii, xii) uses `IsWeaklyRegular` for each system of parameters plus m•W ≠ W stated separately, as in the notes; given m•W ≠ W this is equivalent to `IsRegular`.

Slot vii: 'F_0 = R' is modelled by an arbitrary isomorphism e : F.complex.X 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of R R and 'lift the identity R = K_0 → F_0 = R' by α.f 0 = (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv) ≫ e.inv; quantifying over all e is equivalent to requiring α.f 0 to be an isomorphism (both amount to α_0 = unit · id, and nonvanishing of α_d is invariant under units). The resolution is a Mathlib `ProjectiveResolution` of the residue field whose terms are all `Module.Free`; finite generation of the F_i is not imposed (the source does not impose it). The Koszul complex is realised as ⋀^n(Fin d → R) with contraction differential; K_d ≅ R is not identified explicitly since the conclusion α.f d ≠ 0 is invariant.

Slot xi: module-finiteness of R ⊆ S is added (per Ranganathan's formulation and the notes); without it the statement is false (e.g. k[[x,y]] → k[[x,t]], y ↦ xt, Q = (t) lying over yR). 'xR is a direct summand of Q as R-modules' is rendered as an R-linear ρ : Q →ₗ[R] span{x} with ρ(x r) = x r on the image of xR in Q; the membership proof h is universally quantified (nonvacuous because of hQx). Height one is `Q.primeHeight = 1`.

Slot xiii: dim M is `Module.supportDim R M` (Mathlib's Krull dimension of a module, equal to dim R/ann M for finitely generated M); in slot iii the literal parenthetical `ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R N)` is used instead. χ(M,N) sums i over Finset.range (d+1) (Tor_i = 0 for i > d over a regular local ring of dim d) and uses `ENat.toNat` on `Module.length`, which is lossless because each Tor_i has finite length when M ⊗ N does. Tor is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat R)`.

Universes: R : Type u and all modules/algebras whose existence is asserted (W in viii, B_R/B_S in xii, M in xiv) live in Type u; f.g. modules can always be taken in Type u, and Hochster's modification construction gives big CM modules in Type u. Tor-based slots (x, xiii) need all rings and modules in one universe.
Complete local ring is `IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R`; local homomorphism is `IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)`.
Slot ix omits an explicit injectivity hypothesis since the R-linear retraction already forces it.

statement_blocks.homological_conjectures_in_commutative_a:
/--
**The Zero Divisor Theorem.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M \neq 0$ a finitely
generated $R$-module of finite projective dimension. If $r \in R$ is not a zero divisor on $M$,
then $r$ is not a zero divisor on $R$.

Proved by Peskine–Szpiro and Roberts (it follows from the New Intersection Theorem).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.i
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : ∃ n : ℕ, HasProjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of R M) n)
    (r : R) (hr : IsSMulRegular M r) :
    IsSMulRegular R r := by
  sorry

/--
**Bass's Question.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring. If there is a finitely generated
$R$-module $M \neq 0$ of finite injective dimension (i.e. admitting a finite injective
resolution), then $R$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring.

Answered positively by Peskine–Szpiro and Roberts.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.ii
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : ∃ n : ℕ, HasInjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of R M) n) :
    IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing R := by
  sorry

/--
**The Intersection Theorem.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M$, $N$ finitely generated
$R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N \neq 0$ has finite length. Then the Krull dimension of $N$,
i.e. $\dim R / \operatorname{Ann}_R N$, is at most the projective dimension of $M$ (the bound
is vacuous if $M$ has infinite projective dimension).

Proved by Peskine–Szpiro and Roberts.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.iii
    (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hMN : Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N)) (hMN' : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N)) :
    ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R N) ≤ projectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R M) := by
  sorry

/--
**The New Intersection Theorem.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and let
$0 \to G_n \to \cdots \to G_0 \to 0$ be a finite complex of finitely generated free $R$-modules
such that $\bigoplus_i H_i(G_\bullet)$ has finite length but is not $0$. Then $\dim R \leq n$.

Proved by Roberts (1987).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.iv
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (G.X i)) (hfin : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (G.X i))
    (hn : ∀ i > n, Subsingleton (G.X i))
    (hlen : ∀ i, IsFiniteLength R (G.homology i)) (hne : ∃ i, Nontrivial (G.homology i)) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/--
**Cohen–Macaulayness of Direct Summands Conjecture.** Let $R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism of
Noetherian rings with $S$ regular, such that $R$ is a direct summand of $S$ as an $R$-module,
i.e. $R \to S$ admits an $R$-linear retraction. Then $R$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring.
$R$ need not be local.

Proved by Heitmann–Ma (2018) using weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.ix
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra R S]
    (hS : IsRegularRing S)
    (hRS : ∃ f : S →ₗ[R] R, f ∘ₗ Algebra.linearMap R S = LinearMap.id) :
    IsCohenMacaulayRing R := by
  sorry

/--
**The Improved New Intersection Conjecture.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and let
$0 \to G_n \to \cdots \to G_0 \to 0$ be a finite complex of finitely generated free $R$-modules
such that $H_i(G_\bullet)$ has finite length for $i > 0$ and $H_0(G_\bullet)$ has a minimal
generator killed by a power of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, i.e. there is
$z \in H_0(G_\bullet) \setminus \mathfrak m_R H_0(G_\bullet)$ with $\mathfrak m_R^k z = 0$ for
some $k$. Then $\dim R \leq n$.

Equivalent to the Canonical Element Conjecture, hence a theorem by André's proof of the
Direct Summand Conjecture.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.v
    (n : ℕ) (G : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (G.X i)) (hfin : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (G.X i))
    (hn : ∀ i > n, Subsingleton (G.X i))
    (hlen : ∀ i > 0, IsFiniteLength R (G.homology i))
    (hgen : ∃ z : G.homology 0, z ∉ maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R (G.homology 0)) ∧
      ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ maximalIdeal R ^ k, r • z = 0) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ n := by
  sorry

/--
**The Direct Summand Conjecture.** Let $R \subseteq S$ be a module-finite ring extension with
$R$ a regular (Noetherian) ring; $R$ need not be local. Then $R$ is a direct summand of $S$ as an
$R$-module, i.e. the inclusion $R \to S$ admits an $R$-linear retraction $S \to R$.

Proved by André using perfectoid spaces [An18].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.vi
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (hR : IsRegularRing R) (hRS : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) :
    ∃ f : S →ₗ[R] R, f ∘ₗ Algebra.linearMap R S = LinearMap.id := by
  sorry

/--
**The Canonical Element Conjecture.** Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$ with
residue field $k$. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_d$ be a system of parameters for $R$, let $F_\bullet$ be a
free $R$-resolution of $k$ with $F_0 = R$, and let $K_\bullet = K_\bullet(x_1, \ldots, x_d; R)$
be the Koszul complex. Lift the identity map $R = K_0 \to F_0 = R$ to a map of complexes
$\alpha \colon K_\bullet \to F_\bullet$. Then, whatever the choice of system of parameters, of
resolution and of lifting, the last map $\alpha_d \colon R = K_d \to F_d$ is not $0$.

Here the identification $F_0 = R$ is an isomorphism `e`, and $K_0 = \bigwedge^0 R^d = R$ is the
canonical isomorphism `exteriorPower.zeroEquiv`; the resolution is a projective resolution all
of whose terms are free.

Equivalent to the Direct Summand Conjecture, hence a theorem by André.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.vii
    {d : ℕ} (x : Fin d → R) (hx : IsSystemOfParameters R (List.ofFn x))
    (F : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R)))
    (hF : ∀ i, Module.Free R (F.complex.X i))
    (e : F.complex.X 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of R R)
    (α : koszulComplex x ⟶ F.complex)
    (hα : α.f 0 =
      ModuleCat.ofHom (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv R (Fin d → R)).toLinearMap ≫ e.inv) :
    α.f d ≠ 0 := by
  sorry

variable (R) in
/--
**Existence of Balanced Big Cohen–Macaulay Modules Conjecture.** For every Noetherian local ring
$R$ there is a (not necessarily finitely generated) $R$-module $W$ such that
$\mathfrak m_R W \neq W$ and every system of parameters for $R$ is a regular sequence on $W$.

Proved by Hochster–Huneke in equal characteristic and by André in mixed characteristic.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.viii :
    ∃ (W : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup W) (_ : Module R W), IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay R W := by
  sorry

/--
**The Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor.** Let $A \subseteq R \to S$ be ring homomorphisms
with $A$ and $S$ regular (Noetherian) rings and $R$ finitely generated as an $A$-module; $R$ need
not be local. Let $W$ be any $A$-module. Then the map
$\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(W, R) \to \operatorname{Tor}_i^A(W, S)$ is zero for all $i \geq 1$.

Known in equal characteristic (Hochster–Huneke), open in mixed characteristic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.x
    (A R S : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra A R] [Algebra A S] [Algebra R S] [IsScalarTower A R S]
    (hA : IsRegularRing A) (hS : IsRegularRing S)
    (hAR : Function.Injective (algebraMap A R)) [Module.Finite A R]
    (W : Type u) [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W] (i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) :
    ((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj (ModuleCat.of A W)).map
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A R S).toLinearMap) = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
**The Strong Direct Summand Conjecture.** Let $R \subseteq S$ be a module-finite extension of
complete (Noetherian) local domains, let $x \in R$ be such that $R$ and $R / xR$ are both regular,
and let $Q$ be a height one prime ideal of $S$ lying over $xR$, i.e. $Q \cap R = xR$. Then $xR$
is a direct summand of $Q$ considered as $R$-modules, i.e. the inclusion $xR \to Q$ admits an
$R$-linear retraction $Q \to xR$.

As in the Direct Summand Conjecture that it strengthens, the extension $R \subseteq S$ is
module-finite (this is explicit in Ranganathan's formulation; without it the statement fails).

Equivalent to the Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor; open in general.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xi
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    (hR : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R) (hS : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S)
    [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S] (hRS : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (x : R) (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing R) (hreg' : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}))
    (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime] (hQ : Q.primeHeight = 1)
    (hQx : Q.comap (algebraMap R S) = Ideal.span {x}) :
    ∃ ρ : Q →ₗ[R] Ideal.span {x},
      ∀ (r : R) (h : algebraMap R S (x * r) ∈ Q),
        (ρ ⟨algebraMap R S (x * r), h⟩ : R) = x * r := by
  sorry

/--
**Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen–Macaulay Algebras Conjecture.** Let $R \to S$ be a
local homomorphism of complete (Noetherian) local domains. Then there exist an $R$-algebra $B_R$
that is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for $R$, an $S$-algebra $B_S$ that is a balanced
big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for $S$, and a ring homomorphism $B_R \to B_S$ such that the square
$R \to S \to B_S$, $R \to B_R \to B_S$ commutes.

Proved by André (2018), with contributions of Heitmann–Ma and Gabber.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xii
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    (hR : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R) (hS : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal S) S)
    [Algebra R S] (hRS : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)) :
    ∃ (B_R : Type u) (_ : CommRing B_R) (_ : Algebra R B_R)
      (B_S : Type u) (_ : CommRing B_S) (_ : Algebra S B_S),
      IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay R B_R ∧ IsBalancedBigCohenMacaulay S B_S ∧
      ∃ f : B_R →+* B_S,
        ∀ r : R, f (algebraMap R B_R r) = algebraMap S B_S (algebraMap R S r) := by
  sorry

/--
**Serre's Conjecture on Multiplicities.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring of dimension $d$ and
$M$, $N$ finitely generated $R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. Let
$\chi(M, N) = \sum_i (-1)^i \ell(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N))$. Then $\chi(M, N) = 0$ if
$\dim M + \dim N < d$, and $\chi(M, N) > 0$ if $\dim M + \dim N = d$.
(Serre proved that $\dim M + \dim N \leq d$ always holds.)

The vanishing part is a theorem of Roberts and Gillet–Soulé; the positivity part is open in
mixed characteristic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xiii
    (hR : IsRegularLocalRing R) (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim R = d)
    (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hMN : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N)) :
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N < d → serreMultiplicity R d M N = 0) ∧
    (Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = d → 0 < serreMultiplicity R d M N) := by
  sorry

/--
**Small Cohen–Macaulay Modules Conjecture.** Let $R$ be a complete Noetherian local ring. Then
there is a finitely generated $R$-module $M \neq 0$ such that some (equivalently, every) system of
parameters for $R$ is a regular sequence on $M$.

Open in dimension at least $3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra.parts.xiv
    (hR : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R) :
    ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M), Module.Finite R M ∧ Nontrivial M ∧
      ∃ rs : List R, IsSystemOfParameters R rs ∧ IsRegular M rs := by
  sorry
